problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Every component f_i is convex on all of R^d; consequently F(x) = (1/n)∑_i f_i(x) is convex. Strong convexity is not required.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The objective is the average of n components, with n ≥ 2.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query chooses any component i and point x and receives the exact gradient ∇f_i(x). Answers are independent of history and oracle seeds. Each component query counts as one oracle call; randomized adaptive algorithms are unrestricted.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ExpectedInterpolatedGeneralizedFiniteSum.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible oracle.answer equality. LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm; Setup.allowedAlgorithm; executeWithTrace.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same component query also returns the exact value f_i(x), jointly with its gradient.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Each component has a differentiable gradient satisfying ‖D(∇f_i)(x)‖ ≤ L0 + L1‖∇f_i(x)‖ globally, with L0 > 0 and L1 ≥ 0. This is a componentwise condition.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ExpectedInterpolatedGeneralizedFiniteSum.lean: spec.admissible gradient differentiability and fderiv bound; spec.valid.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is Euclidean R^d, with d ≥ ⌈2^80(1 + n + L1 R + L0 R²/ε)^24⌉.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Interpolation: there exists a common global minimizer xstar of every component, with ‖xstar‖ ≤ R and F(0) − F(xstar) ≤ Δ. All parameters d, n, L0, L1, R, Δ, ε are public; the component functions and minimizer are hidden. The regime requires R > 0, ε > 0, 2ε ≤ Δ, and 4nε ≤ L0 R².
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ExpectedInterpolatedGeneralizedFiniteSum.lean: Params; spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.valid, spec.admissible common-minimizer condition.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The algorithm outputs a point xhat in R^d. For a common component minimizer xstar, the objective gap must be integrable and satisfy E[F(xhat) − F(xstar)] ≤ ε. No last-iterate or queried-point restriction is imposed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Accuracy is in expectation over algorithm and oracle seeds; exact oracle answers make oracle randomness immaterial. The supplied lower-bound budget counts a fixed cap on component value-and-gradient queries.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ExpectedInterpolatedGeneralizedFiniteSum.lean: spec.successful; spec.admissible oracle equality. LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm.law; executeWithTrace; Convergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: This meaningful variant combines convex finite sums and exact component queries with componentwise gradient-dependent smoothness, a common component minimizer, and a prescribed large-dimension regime.

descriptionHtml:
Interpolated Generalized Smooth Finite Sums

We consider minimizing F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x) on Euclidean space Rd, where n≥2 is the number of components and d is the dimension. Each fi:Rd→R is convex and (L0,L1)-smooth, with L0>0 and L1≥0, and has a differentiable gradient. The components share a minimizer x⋆ satisfying ∥x⋆∥≤R and F(0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ, where R>0 and Δ>0. At a queried pair (i,x), the oracle returns (fi(x),∇fi(x)). For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯ with integrable objective gap satisfying EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈RdF(x). We use the Euclidean norm and its induced operator norms, denoted by ∥⋅∥ and ∥⋅∥op, respectively. The algorithm receives all parameters d,n,L0,L1,R,Δ,ε; the component functions are accessed through the oracle. The parameter regime is n,d∈N,n≥2,L0>0,L1≥0,R>0,ε>0,2ε≤Δ,4nε≤L0R2,d≥⌈280(1+n+L1R+L0R2ε)24⌉.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Component convexity). For every i∈{1,…,n}, x,y∈Rd, and t∈[0,1], fi((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)fi(x)+tfi(y).

Assumption 2 (Generalized smoothness). Each fi is differentiable everywhere, and ∇fi:Rd→Rd is Fréchet differentiable everywhere. Its Hessian satisfies ∥∇2fi(x)∥op≤L0+L1∥∇fi(x)∥,i∈{1,…,n},x∈Rd.

Assumption 3 (Interpolation and reference bounds). There exists x⋆∈Rd such that fi(x⋆)≤fi(x)for every i∈{1,…,n}, x∈Rd,∥x⋆∥≤R,F(0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ. The origin is a reference point for these bounds, rather than a prescribed algorithm initialization.

Each oracle call selects any component i∈{1,…,n} and any point x∈Rd and returns the exact pair (fi(x),∇fi(x)). After the allotted calls, the output x¯∈Rd must satisfy EP[|F(x¯)−F(x⋆)|]<∞,EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε. Here x⋆ is a fixed common minimizer of the components; all such minimizers have the same value of F.

comparisonHtml:
F=n−1∑i=1nfi on Rd, with convex components having differentiable gradients and ∥∇2fi(x)∥≤L0+L1∥∇fi(x)∥. A common minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x⋆∥≤R and F(0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ. Parameters satisfy L0,R,ε>0, L1≥0, n≥2, Δ≥2ε, L0R2/ε≥4n, and d≥⌈280(1+n+L1R+L0R2/ε)24⌉. The target is an integrable gap with ∫[F(x^(ω))−F(x⋆)]dP(ω)≤ε, where P is the algorithm’s seed law. Hardness holds against every randomized adaptive algorithm using exact component value/gradient pairs, at every fixed budget through the stated threshold; the instance is independent of the realized seed.

Lower bounds (necessary budgets) for ExpectedInterpolatedGeneralizedFiniteSum.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) ExpectedInterpolatedGeneralizedFiniteSumLowerBound (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) Necessary: Ω(n(1+q2/3)+n(H+q)log2⁡(2+n+q+H)) component calls.
(2) (Rudomanov et al. 2026, Thm. 7.1, v2) Necessary: Ω(n(1+q2/3)+n[H+q2(1+δ/ε)]log2⁡(2+n+H+q2(1+δ/ε))) value/gradient calls. Requires q>0, δ≥3ε/q2; no interpolation guarantee. (1): Scope: all four terms persist at δ=0; matches (2) at δ=3ε/q2, and includes L1=0. (1) requires H≥4n and the explicit large polynomial dimension; fixed-budget hardness rather than expected-stopping-time hardness.
(3) (Woodworth and Srebro 2019, Thm. 7, v3). Smooth convex components on a radius-R ball; L1=0, without interpolation. Necessary: Ω(n+nH) component value/gradient/prox calls, in sufficiently large dimension. (1): Scope: hardness with a common minimizer; adds the L1>0 terms. At L1=0, (1) loses log2⁡(2+n+H), excludes prox queries, and requires H≥4n.

Abbr: n: component count; H=L0R2/ε; q=L1R; δ: upper bound on minF−n−1∑iinffi; Ω: necessary calls, up to universal factors. A component call returns the value and gradient together; (3) additionally permits a component proximal evaluation.

source:
import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic

namespace LongTails.Setups.ExpectedInterpolatedGeneralizedFiniteSum

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  n : ℕ
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev Point (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)

noncomputable def objective {p : Params} (f : Fin p.n → Point p → ℝ) (x : Point p) : ℝ :=
  (p.n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, f i x

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Fin p.n → Point p → ℝ
  Query p := Fin p.n × Point p
  Reply p := ℝ × Point p
  Output p := Point p
  publicInput := id
  valid p := 0 < p.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ p.L1 ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ 2 ≤ p.n ∧
    2 * p.ε ≤ p.Δ ∧ 4 * p.n * p.ε ≤ p.L0 * p.R ^ 2 ∧
    ⌈(2 : ℝ) ^ 80 * (1 + p.n + p.L1 * p.R + p.L0 * p.R ^ 2 / p.ε) ^ 24⌉₊ ≤ p.d
  admissible p f oracle :=
    (∀ i, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (f i)) ∧
    (∀ i x, HasGradientAt (f i) (gradient (f i) x) x) ∧
    (∀ i, Differentiable ℝ (gradient (f i))) ∧
    (∀ i x, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient (f i)) x‖ ≤ p.L0 + p.L1 * ‖gradient (f i) x‖) ∧
    (∀ history seed i x, oracle.answer history (0, (i, x)) seed = (f i x, gradient (f i) x)) ∧
    ∃ xstar, (∀ i, IsMinOn (f i) Set.univ xstar) ∧ ‖xstar‖ ≤ p.R ∧
      objective f 0 - objective f xstar ≤ p.Δ
  successful p f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, (∀ i, IsMinOn (f i) Set.univ xstar) ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => objective f (output ω) - objective f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, objective f (output ω) - objective f xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.ExpectedInterpolatedGeneralizedFiniteSum
